history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Build both pandas revisions with the same compiled recipe (Cython extensions in pandas/_libs/window/aggregations.pyx), then run the developer test pandas/tests/window/test_rolling.py -k test_rolling_var_numerical_issues on each, so it fails on buggy (assertion mismatch on var/std values) and passes on fixed. Test file and tolerances are untouched.
assumptions: No Python version is stated in the context; the default interpreter of the harness is assumed to be suitable, so python_version is omitted (inferred, not stated).
No numpy pin is applied because no documented constraint or era ceiling is given; numpy is left unbounded (inferred choice).
The PR date is blank, so no date-based pin was chosen.

The 'native_library_failure' diagnosis is read as a build-stage concern handled by the compiled rebuild; if the build fails, the next iteration should inspect the compiler/build output and adjust the build configuration, not the test.

actions.step: Build buggy and fixed with the same compiled recipe (pandas has Cython extensions; editable build with --no-build-isolation per environment.build_commands).
Verify the developer test FAILS on the buggy revision with a real assertion failure (not collection/import error).
Verify the developer test PASSES on the fixed revision.

plans.success_criterion: On buggy, pytest reports test_rolling_var_numerical_issues FAILED with an assertion from tm.assert_series_equal on the rolling var/std output (not a collection, import, or build error); on fixed, the same selection PASSES; both use the same built environment recipe and the unmodified developer test.
